title.narrative: Strengthen Public Health Surveillance, Early Warning, and Prevention and Control of Communicable Diseases in the Gaza Strip - 2026

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project will strengthen laboratory diagnostic and disease surveillance capacities in Gaza to improve the detection, confirmation, and response to priority communicable diseases and antimicrobial-resistant infections. ltbrgtltbrgtThe project will reactivate microbiology laboratory services through the procurement and distribution of essential laboratory consumables and supplies for bacteriology and microbiology testing. This will enable accurate diagnosis and strengthen antimicrobial resistance (AMR) detection and monitoring, enabling the management of an estimated 4,000 patients, including those requiring trauma-related and limb reconstructive care. ltbrgtltbrgtTo support timely outbreak detection and verification, the project will also restore core functionality of the health laboratory network by providing essential consumables and rapid diagnostic test kits for priority diseases, strengthening laboratory confirmation capacity across outbreak-prone conditions. ltbrgtltbrgtIn parallel, the project will scale up and strengthen the Early Warning, Alert and Response System (EWARS) to improve surveillance sensitivity and timeliness. Key outputs include the onboarding of 20 surveillance focal points from health facilities refresher training for 150 EWARS health-facility focal points and geo-administrators on reportable diseases, data quality, and alert verification sensitization of 1,000 clinicians to improve early case detection and reporting and quarterly governorate-level reviews of surveillance performance indicators. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtIn addition, the project will strengthen infection prevention and control (IPC), and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) measures at health facilities. Key outputs include the training of 38 WASH laboratories and environmental inspectors, and 1,910 health facility staff in IPC to reduce the risk of infection-related morbidities and mortality for health care providers and those seeking care, related to the lack of WASH services, critical to maintaining the ability to provide essential safe and quality care.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtCollectively, these outputs will enhance diagnostic and surveillance capacity, improve timely response to public health threats, and contribute to improved patient outcomes and strengthened health system resilience in Gaza. ltbrgtlt/pgt
